latin: Christus in ultimo iudicio iudicabit non solum in natura humana, sed
latin_note: Farmer's inventory line breaks off mid-sentence at 'sed', but Edelheit quotes the complete printed thesis, citing 'Pico, 900 Theses, page 224', as 'Christus in ultimo iudicio iudicabit non solum in natura humana, sed etiam secundum naturam humanam' (edelheit2022:11023).
translation: At the last judgment Christ will judge not only in human nature, but also according to human nature.
translation_note: Farmer's own note (paraphrased, not reproduced) glosses the thesis in the same terms: Christ in the Last Judgment will judge not only in human nature but also according to human nature (farmer1998:11589).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch3, from Latin at farmer1998:11525

sources.text: Thomas Aquinas, Scriptum super Sententiis, book 4, distinction 48, question 1, article 1
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit identifies this as the location of Thomas's discussion behind the thesis

doctrine: The thesis distinguishes Christ judging 'in' human nature (as possessing it) from judging 'according to' human nature (as its exercised standard), a distinction Edelheit locates in Thomas's commentary on the Sentences, book 4, distinction 48, question 1, article 1 (edelheit2022:11000). Edelheit remarks that, as it stands, the thesis 'does not make much sense without an explanation', while also judging it 'an accurate conclusion' relative to Thomas's discussion (edelheit2022:11000).
context: Edelheit frames the thesis as part of a set that does not exhaust the theological nuance found in Thomas, adding that the project of the 900 Theses was not wholly a work of scholastic theology and that Pico was not a professional theologian (edelheit2022:11000).
historiography: Edelheit is the only scholar found discussing this thesis in the sources consulted; he judges Pico's formulation compressed to the point of needing explanation, yet substantively accurate to Thomas's own discussion (edelheit2022:11000).

quotations.text: Thesis 16 states that Christ in the final judgement will judge not only in human nature but also according to human nature.
Christus in ultimo iudicio iudicabit non solum in natura humana, sed etiam secundum naturam humanam.
